source: Lincolnshire CC 2026/27 budget (ModernGov lincolnshire.moderngov.co.uk docs s72426 + s71846, full Council 20 Feb 2026, verified by pdftotext) + the AI DOGE directorate engine.

directorates.name: Fire and Rescue
directorates._note: Lincolnshire runs its own county Fire and Rescue Service.

cross_cutting._note: GBP 35.5m of new savings in 2026/27 (Table A2 verified); engine risk-adjusts to ~GBP 21.06m EV. Directorate split is a net-budget-weighted allocation (flagged); line-item annex in s72426 section 5.

mtfs_period: 2026/27 balanced; deficit rising to GBP 55.6m by 2028/29 (Budget Setting Report)

reserves._note: General reserves held at 2.5%-3.5% of net budget; GBP 2m use for non-recurrent drainage; core budget does not draw on general or volatility reserves. Usable reserves total not separately extracted.

risks.risk: DSG High Needs goes into structural deficit for the FIRST time in 2025/26 (Q2 overspend GBP 26.4m). The DfE national mechanism resolves 90% of DSG deficits accrued to end 2025/26, but the statutory override ends at the end of 2027/28, after which the council could not offset DSG deficits against general funds. Lincolnshire is not headlined as a Safety Valve authority.

Medium-term financial plan deficit rising to GBP 55.6m by 2028/29 against GBP 82.6m of 2026/27 cost pressures (Adult Care +32.9m, Children in Care +14.7m); GBP 62.7m of new savings identified across the MTFP. Reliant on fair-funding gains phased over three years.
Adult Care and Community Wellbeing (GBP 360.9m, the dominant spend) carries the bulk of the savings against rising demand; delivery risk concentrated in adult social care.
